manifest.name: Unsplash Image Library
manifest.summary: Find free high-resolution images from Unsplash
manifest.author: Odoo S.A.

models._description: General Settings (extension): adds Unsplash app id / access key

behavioral_notes.observation: Server-side proxy to the Unsplash search API. Reads the access_key (ir.config_parameter 'unsplash.access_key') and app_id ('unsplash.app_id') via sudo(); if either is missing it returns {'error':'key_not_found'} (for managers) or {'error':'no_access'} (for non-managers, gated by res.users._can_manage_unsplash_settings). When configured it injects client_id=access_key into the POST params and does requests.get('https://api.unsplash.com/search/photos/'), relaying the raw Unsplash JSON to the browser. The key never reaches the client; the browser only ever sees search results. Metadata-invisible outbound HTTP call.

Materialises a chosen Unsplash photo into a local ir.attachment. For each {url, download_url, description} it validates the URL host is images.unsplash.com / plus.unsplash.com, requests.get()s the binary, runs image_process(verify_resolution=True) + guess_mimetype, then delegates to html_editor's HTML_Editor._attachment_create to build the attachment named 'unsplash_<id>_<query>'. It then sudo()-sets attachment.url to '/unsplash/<id>/<query>' (deliberately bypassing _check_serving_attachments, which normally forbids a binary attachment having a URL) and generate_access_token(). Returns attachment._get_media_info() to the editor. Side effect: a free stock photo becomes an owned, servable record on res_model/res_id (default ir.ui.view).

After each image is saved, _notify_download(download_url) pings the photo's Unsplash download_url with client_id=access_key. This is mandated by Unsplash API guidelines (it increments the photographer's download counter) and is required to stay compliant with their terms; failures are swallowed and logged, never surfaced to the user. The URL is validated to start with 'https://api.unsplash.com/photos/'. Pure side-effect of a third-party compliance obligation, not in any model.

API credentials are not module data: they are stored as ir.config_parameter rows 'unsplash.access_key' and 'unsplash.app_id', surfaced as config_parameter Char fields on res.config.settings (General Settings). The /web_unsplash/save_unsplash route lets a website restricted editor or ERP manager (res.users._can_manage_unsplash_settings: base.group_erp_manager OR website.group_website_restricted_editor) set them at runtime without the Settings form, raising NotFound otherwise. So the integration is keyed per-database via system parameters, configured by privileged users only.

Extends the QWeb image field converter so that when website/editor HTML containing an is saved back, from_html() resolves the local public ir.attachment (matched by url path + res_model/res_id) and returns its datas, instead of re-fetching from Unsplash. This stitches the saved stock photo into Odoo's normal image-serving pipeline.

web_unsplash is an outbound third-party integration: controllers/main.py uses the `requests` library against https://api.unsplash.com/search/photos/ (search), https://api.unsplash.com/photos/ (download notify), and downloads binaries from https://images.unsplash.com/ / https://plus.unsplash.com/. Authentication is an Unsplash Access Key (client_id) held in ir.config_parameter. None of these HTTP call-sites or the api-key dependency are visible in Python ORM metadata.

it_architecture.application: web_unsplash (Unsplash image-search/insert integration for the HTML editor & website; outbound Unsplash API proxy)
logical_data_erm: web_unsplash -> ir.attachment (downloaded image stored as attachment, url=/unsplash/<id>/<query>)
ir.qweb.field.image.from_html -> ir.attachment (resolve saved /unsplash/ image by url + res_model/res_id)
information_flows: search: OWL ImageSelector/MediaDialog -> /web_unsplash/fetch_images -> requests.get(api.unsplash.com/search/photos) -> JSON results to browser
insert: editor -> /web_unsplash/attachment/add -> requests.get(images.unsplash.com binary) -> image_process -> HTML_Editor._attachment_create -> ir.attachment(url=/unsplash/...)
config: General Settings / save_unsplash -> ir.config_parameter(unsplash.access_key, unsplash.app_id)
render: saved HTML -> ir.qweb.field.image.from_html -> attachment.datas
frontend_components: UnsplashCredentials (OWL: app id / access key entry for privileged users)
UnsplashError (OWL: surfaces no_access / key_not_found / API errors)
unsplash service (registry services:unsplash — client-side search/save orchestration)
unsplash_beacon (public.interactions: Unsplash download-tracking beacon on the public website)

capabilities: Search free stock imagery from an external provider (Unsplash) inside the editor
Insert / download a chosen stock photo as a local managed attachment
Honour external-provider API compliance (download attribution callback)
value_streams: Find-to-Insert media: open media dialog -> search Unsplash -> pick image -> download to ir.attachment -> embed in page/record
Configure-integration: privileged user enters app id + access key -> stored as config parameters -> integration enabled
policies: res.users._can_manage_unsplash_settings: only base.group_erp_manager OR website.group_website_restricted_editor may set credentials / see key-config errors
URL allow-listing: only images.unsplash.com / plus.unsplash.com binaries and api.unsplash.com/photos/ notify URLs are accepted (server-side validation)
Mandatory Unsplash download-notification callback per Unsplash API terms
stakeholders: Website editor / content author (searches & inserts stock photos)
ERP manager / website restricted editor (configures API credentials)
metrics: Unsplash download-notification beacon (per-image download count reported back to Unsplash)

classification.rationale: web_unsplash is firm IT/content infrastructure (Porter support activity; Stabell & Fjeldstad 'support'), not a value-creating primary activity of any chain/shop/network. It is a thin media-tooling bridge that lets the html_editor and website pull free stock imagery from an external API: 0 business models (only 3 inherit-only extensions), 4 jsonrpc routes, ~355 Python LOC, and its real substance is an external integration (gap #7: requests against api.unsplash.com / images.unsplash.com, an api-key in ir.config_parameter) plus an OWL/JS image-picker UI patched into MediaDialog/ImageSelector (gap #3). auto_install=true makes it ubiquitous editor plumbing. APQC 8.0 'Manage Information Technology' fits because the work is IT delivery — develop/manage application software and integrate an external content/media service into the platform; 4.x/5.x (operations/marketing) were rejected because the module performs no primary operating activity, it only equips other modules' UIs with a media source.

standard_capabilities: Unsplash search tab inside the editor/website MediaDialog image picker
One-click download of a free high-res photo into a local ir.attachment
API credentials (app id + access key) configured in General Settings, stored as system parameters
Automatic Unsplash download-notification callback to stay API-terms compliant
Public-website beacon + QWeb rendering of saved /unsplash/ images
typical_fits: Adding royalty-free imagery to website pages, blog posts, products, mail templates via the standard editor
Centrally provisioning one Unsplash account per database for all editors
No-code enablement: paste keys in Settings, feature appears in the media dialog
common_gaps: Custom image providers beyond Unsplash require JS dev (patch MediaDialog/ImageSelector, new service — gap #3)
Unsplash account/keys must be provisioned externally (not shipped); rate limits & terms are the provider's
No local caching/dedup beyond the per-insert ir.attachment; no usage governance UI
Credential errors only actionable by erp-manager / website-restricted-editor users
drive_hints: curl -X POST /web_unsplash/fetch_images (auth=user) with {query:'lion',page:1,per_page:5} -> proxied Unsplash search JSON (or {'error':...} if unkeyed)
In website/editor: open Insert Media -> Images -> Unsplash tab, search a term, click an image -> inspect the created ir.attachment (url starts /unsplash/)
odoo shell: env['ir.attachment'].search([('url','=like','/unsplash/%')]) to list materialised Unsplash images

open_questions: Unsplash rate-limit / quota behaviour and how exhaustion surfaces in the UI (not in code, depends on provider plan).
Whether downloaded attachments are deduplicated across pages/records (each insert creates a fresh ir.attachment).
Exact client-side flow of the OWL 'unsplash' service and the public unsplash_beacon interaction (JS, gap #3 — not in Python metadata).
